skill.name: k8s-security-policies
skill.description: Create and review Kubernetes NetworkPolicy, Pod Security Standards, RBAC, admission control, and service mesh security examples for production clusters.
skill.summary: Create Kubernetes security policies for network isolation, pod hardening, RBAC, and admission control.
skill.author: wshobson

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown code fences, YAML examples, inline references, or fixed kubectl troubleshooting commands. The broad HTTPS egress template is a real policy risk. Overbroad RBAC examples could expand secret or admin access if copied into production. No prompt injection attempt was found.

remediation.suggestion: Replace the open CIDR example with named destination guidance, namespace-scoped egress examples, or a warning to restrict approved endpoints.

remediation.issue: RBAC examples grant broad secret and wildcard administrative permissions.
remediation.suggestion: Use namespace-scoped Roles, resourceNames, specific resources, and minimal verbs in default examples. Mark any admin role as break-glass only.

remediation.issue: Markdown fences triggered external command detection.
remediation.suggestion: Keep examples clearly labeled as documentation and avoid unnecessary shell snippets unless the command is required for troubleshooting.

semantic_findings.title: Overbroad RBAC Examples
semantic_findings.description: The guide includes a cluster-wide secret-reader ClusterRole and a namespace-admin Role with wildcard resources and verbs. Users may copy these examples into production, expanding secret exposure and administrative access.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited examples directly grant broad secret access and wildcard namespace permissions. The surrounding material includes least-privilege advice, so this is a risky guidance issue rather than clear malicious intent.

content.value_statement: Kubernetes teams need clear policy examples that reduce network and permission risk. This skill provides reusable guidance for NetworkPolicy, Pod Security Standards, RBAC, admission control, and service mesh security.
actual_capabilities: Provides NetworkPolicy templates for default deny, DNS, service access, ingress, monitoring, external HTTPS, database, and cross-namespace traffic.
Explains namespace Pod Security Standards labels for privileged, baseline, and restricted modes.
Shows RBAC Roles, ClusterRoles, RoleBindings, ServiceAccount patterns, and permission troubleshooting commands.
Includes OPA Gatekeeper and Istio security policy examples.
Summarizes CIS and NIST-aligned Kubernetes security practices.
limitations: Does not inspect a live cluster or verify policies against deployed workloads.
Examples require adaptation for namespace names, labels, ports, and CNI behavior.
Some RBAC examples are broad and should be narrowed before production use.
Does not replace admission testing, threat modeling, or compliance review.

use_cases.title: Build a Namespace Security Baseline
use_cases.description: Create starting policies for pod restrictions, default deny networking, DNS egress, and approved service communication.

use_cases.title: Review Access Controls
use_cases.description: Compare RBAC examples against least-privilege goals and identify permissions that need narrower resources or verbs.

use_cases.title: Troubleshoot Policy Failures
use_cases.description: Use the included checks to investigate denied traffic, missing CNI enforcement, and unexpected RBAC permission failures.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Default Deny Baseline
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me design a default deny NetworkPolicy baseline for namespace <namespace>. Include DNS egress and explain which labels I must replace.

prompt_templates.title: Harden a Workload Namespace
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Kubernetes security plan for a frontend, backend, and database namespace. Cover Pod Security Standards, NetworkPolicy, and least-privilege RBAC.

prompt_templates.title: Review Existing Permissions
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these RBAC rules for production risk. Identify wildcard verbs, secret access, cluster scope, and safer least-privilege replacements.

prompt_templates.title: Design Multi-Tenant Controls
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a multi-tenant Kubernetes security baseline using NetworkPolicy, restricted pod settings, OPA Gatekeeper, audit logging, and service mesh authorization.

output_examples.input: Need a secure starting point for a new production namespace.
output: A default deny networking plan for ingress and egress.
A DNS egress exception and service-specific allow rules.
Restricted pod settings and least-privilege RBAC review notes.

output_examples.input: Need to understand why a service cannot reach its database.
output: A checklist for CNI support, pod labels, namespace selectors, and database port rules.
Suggested permission checks for the workload service account.
Common policy gaps to verify before changing production access.

output_examples.input: Need to reduce risky RBAC in a shared cluster.
output: A review of broad verbs, secret access, and cluster-scoped grants.
Recommendations to use Roles, resourceNames, and dedicated ServiceAccounts.
A migration plan from broad admin access to task-specific permissions.

best_practices: Start with default deny network policies, then add only required DNS, service, and external egress paths.
Use restricted Pod Security Standards for production namespaces unless a documented exception is approved.
Prefer namespace Roles, specific resources, minimal verbs, and dedicated ServiceAccounts for every workload.
anti_patterns: Applying sample policies without changing namespaces, labels, ports, and workload selectors.
Granting wildcard RBAC verbs or broad secret access to application service accounts.
Assuming NetworkPolicy is enforced without confirming that the cluster CNI supports it.

faq.question: Can this skill apply policies to my cluster?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples. You must review, test, and apply policies with your own Kubernetes tooling.

faq.question: Does it support Pod Security Standards?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes namespace label examples for privileged, baseline, and restricted enforcement modes.

faq.question: Does it replace a Kubernetes security audit?
faq.answer: No. It is a starting point for policy design and review, not a complete audit of a live environment.

faq.question: What should I customize before using the examples?
faq.answer: Customize namespaces, labels, ports, service accounts, resource names, and approved external destinations.

faq.question: Why are broad RBAC examples risky?
faq.answer: Broad verbs, wildcard resources, and secret access can expose sensitive data or expand privileges beyond the workload need.

faq.question: Does NetworkPolicy work in every Kubernetes cluster?
faq.answer: No. Enforcement depends on the cluster CNI. Confirm CNI support before relying on NetworkPolicy for isolation.
